Read the files fully.\n\nFILES:\n- sigil/ui/server.py (UIServer + Handler: two-plane auth _token_ok/_action_ok, GET read plane, POST action plane, SSE, provenance /api/record, /api/ask relay)\n- sigil/ui/actions.py (do_action — the owner-signed broker)\n- sigil/ui/static/index.html (the served page; token injection; the JS)\n- tests/test_ui.py (are any assertions greenwashed?)\n\nCLAIM 1 (HIGHEST) — no web page or cross-origin caller can trigger a gated ACTION (approve/deny/kill/release/promote/revoke). Attack:\n- A malicious page on the user's machine (another localhost origin, or a remote page) hitting POST /api/action: can it pass _action_ok? Can a form POST (simple request, no preflight) reach it? Does the custom X-SIGIL-Token header force a CORS preflight that the server rejects cross-origin (there are NO CORS headers — so browsers block the RESPONSE, but does the request still execute the action server-side)? Can any cross-origin page READ the token (the page is same-origin-only; confirm no CORS exposes it)? Is hmac.compare_digest used (timing)?\n- Host allowlist: does a DNS-rebinding Host (evil.com→127.0.0.1) get refused? Does it RE-VERIFY (integrity_ok flips to False on a tampered atom) or trust? Absent record → honest 404, not fabricated?\n- /api/ask relays to KernelDispatch.send(argv) — command injection via the q param (argv list, no shell=True)? Does it egress or take any action beyond a gated KERNEL query?\n\nCLAIM 3 — robustness/honesty: the action plane never 500-leaks internals; SSE is read-only (server→browser only) and not a DoS; the owner key never reaches the browser. Attack:\n- POST /api/action with malformed/huge body, missing fields, a huge Content-Length, wrong types → does it 400 cleanly or crash/500/hang? Does the server ever WRITE state from an SSE/GET (it must not)? \n- Does do_action ever send the private key or sign with a caller-supplied key (it must use the persisted owner identity only)?\n\nFor each objection: file:line, concrete repro, severity, fix hint. {"parentUuid":"8a3df36a-a75f-4170-8db2-89aa1fc4f6f4","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"ffbb8a8a-4bb8-4c99-a79e-9ed4dd97a041","agentId":"a1828ba6a2e9b991d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<command-message>crucible</command-message>\n<command-name>crucible</command-name>\n<skill-format>true</skill-format>"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main/.claude/skills/crucible\n\n# CRUCIBLE — operating the engine\n\nCRUCIBLE turns an authorized seed URL into **oracle-confirmed** findings, reasons over them,\nand produces auditable reports — inside a fail-closed safety stack. Its whole value is one\nrule; internalize it before anything else:\n\n> **A claim is a FACT only when a deterministic oracle fires over data a real target\n> produced.** You (the LLM) ADVISE where to look and what a result might mean; the oracle\n> CONFIRMS. Nothing else — not your confidence, not a critic's endorsement, not a plausible\n> story — promotes a claim to a fact.\n\nThe standing doctrine every reasoning call operates under is\n[framework/cognitive/metacognition.md](../../../framework/cognitive/metacognition.md) (it is\ninjected into every LLM system prompt). The full architecture — agents, event spine, veracity\nlayer, learning/metacognition core, safety stack — is\n[framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md](../../../framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md). The binding\nconstitution is [CLAUDE.md](../../../CLAUDE.md); never relax scope, destruction, evidence, or\nhonesty rules.\n\n## The invariants (never violate these)\n\n1. **Oracle authority.** Only a fired oracle confirms. Critics/RL/reflection/self-consistency\n   may only *advise, re-rank, defer, or abstain* — never promote a finding or override the oracle.\n2. **Coverage.** Never silently skip an authorized attack surface. Learning and reflection\n   *deprioritise* (re-rank / defer); they never gate a surface out.\n3. **Prove by re-execution.** A finding is a fact only if its retained `oracle_context`\n   re-fires. The veracity firewall (`framework/v2/veracity/`) re-runs proofs; it can only demote.\n4. **Non-circular learning.** An EXPLOITABLE label needs ≥2 independent corroborating oracle\n   kinds; a silent oracle is never auto-labelled a false positive.\n5. **Refuse honestly, fail closed.** Decline to conclude what you cannot ground; record every\n   refusal as evidence. Hard limits (scope, authorization, destruction, real user data) are\n   inviolable — when unsure, stop and ask.\n6. **Determinism + append-only.** No wallclock/global-rng in learning/reward math; the event\n   spine is append-only (supersede, never edit).\n\n## Structured workflows\n\n### Run an authorized engagement (end-to-end, gated)\n1. Confirm the active target's `targets/<slug>/charter.md` authorizes it (constitution §II).\n2. `python3 -m framework.v2 engage <slug> <seed-url> [--recon] [--spine]`\n   — crawls, audits, confirms via oracles, chains attack paths, scores confidence, and\n   (with `--spine`) mirrors the whole run onto the immutable blackboard event stream.\n   (`--strict-evidence` is a **`scan`**-only flag, below — not an `engage` flag.)\n3. Every request passes the full gate chain; an out-of-scope seed or tripped kill-switch\n   refuses *before* traffic and is recorded as a `refusal` event.\n\n### Loopback-only quick scan\n`python3 -m framework.v2 scan http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ --format json|sarif|html [--strict-evidence]`\n— the export states each finding's **live grounding** (fact / ungrounded / contradicted);\n`--strict-evidence` withholds non-fact findings from the rendered doc but keeps them in\n`--reverifiable-out`.\n\n### Re-verify a report (prove-don't-guess, offline)\n`python3 -m framework.v2 verify <report.json>` re-runs each finding's retained `oracle_context`.\n`python3 -m framework.v2 evidence ...` builds/verifies signed, hash-linked evidence certificates\n(and, with report claims bound in, fails closed when a report sentence has no backing evidence).\n\n### Inspect / audit the event spine\nThe blackboard (`framework/v2/agents/blackboard.py`) is the one append-only, typed, provenance-\nlinked event stream. Replay it with `Blackboard.replay(engagement=..., since_id=...)`.\nCryptographic tamper-evidence: `framework/v2/agents/spine_chain.py`\n(`build_spine_chain` / `sign_spine_head` / `verify_spine_head`).\n\n### Recon / intel, memory, self-improvement\n`python3 -m framework.v2 intel ...` (OSINT into the shared world-model; gated egress),\n`memory ...` (cross-engagement priors — never fabricate a score), `improve ...`\n(authorise-not-apply — it never self-applies a change).\n\n### Read-only operator console\n`python3 -m framework.v2 console` — loopback, read-only, zero-impact operator UI over the run.\n\n## What NOT to do\n- Do not build detection-evasion / identity-rotation / stay-hidden-from-defenders capability —\n  CRUCIBLE is correlatable and authorized by doctrine (constitution §VI).\n- Do not let any learned/critic/LLM signal enter the deterministic oracle/SCE/calibration inputs\n  or promote a finding.\n- Do not attack third parties (payment/IdP/CDN) — test only the operator's integration with them.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"uuid":"0826b06b-601e-4af0-a5d6-6804db424d74","timestamp":"2026-07-18T19:04:28.426Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Mirrors the MCP server's posture: read-only over the spine +\n3\tprovenance on every atom, plus a CSRF-proof owner-signed action plane.\n4\t\n5\tSecurity model (the red-pen keystone):\n6\t  • binds 127.0.0.1 ONLY (never 0.0.0.0/public).\n7\t  • a session TOKEN is minted at startup and PRINTED TO THE TERMINAL (so only someone at the machine\n8\t    can drive it, and no web page can read it). Recognized text is routed through the Phase-1 KERNEL (`sigil-kernel\n     2\task`), so a voice request crosses the SAME T0 router + WARDEN gate + signed action log as any\n     3\tother — voice is just another interface onto the one authorized path. The spoken response is the\n     4\tKERNEL's answer body (the bracketed [T0…]/[WARDEN…] status lines are stripped).\"\"\"\n     5\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     6\t\n     7\timport subprocess\n     8\tfrom pathlib import Path\n     9\t\n    10\t\n    11\tdef _default_bin() -> str:\n    12\t    for p in (\"kernel/target/release/sigil-kernel\", \"kernel/target/debug/sigil-kernel\"):\n    13\t        f = Path(\"/home/kali/sigil\") / p\n    14\t        if f.exists():\n    15\t            return str(f)\n    16\t    return \"sigil-kernel\"\n    17\t\n    18\t\n    19\tclass KernelDispatch:\n    20\t    def __init__(self, kernel_bin: str | None = None, timeout: int = 60):\n    21\t        self.kernel_bin = kernel_bin or _default_bin()\n    22\t        self.timeout = timeout\n    23\t\n    24\t    # exact KERNEL status-line prefixes to strip (so a legitimate answer line that merely starts\n    25\t    # with '[' is NOT dropped, and a BLOCKED/error is NOT masked as an answer).\n    26\t    _STATUS = (\"[t0\", \"[warden\", \"[blocked\", \"[direct\", \"[dispatch\")\n    27\t\n    28\t    def send(self, text: str) -> str:\n    29\t        text = (text or \"\").strip()\n    30\t        if not text:\n    31\t            return \"I didn't catch that.\"\n    32\t        try:\n    33\t            proc = subprocess.run([self.kernel_bin, \"ask\", text],\n    34\t                                  capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=self.timeout)\n    35\t        except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError) as e:\n    36\t            return f\"the kernel is unavailable ({e})\"\n    37\t        if proc.returncode != 0:\n    38\t            tail = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout).strip().splitlines()\n    39\t            return f\"that request was refused or errored: {tail[-1][:200]}\" if tail else \"that request was refused.\"\n    40\t        if any(ln.lstrip().lower().startswith(\"[blocked\") for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines()):\n    41\t            return \"that action needs your approval — it wasn't run.\"\n    42\t        body = [ln.strip() for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines()\n    43\t                if ln.strip() and not any(ln.lstrip().lower().startswith(s) for s in self._STATUS)]\n    44\t        answer = \" \".join(body).strip()\n    45\t        return answer[:600] if answer else \"there's no answer for that in memory yet.\"\n===== sigil/spine/verify.py =====\n     1\t\"\"\"verify_record (Phase 7, P0.2) — the single \"prove-this-atom\" helper reused by the live tail,\n     2\tthe UI `/api/record` endpoint, and the mobile daemon, so \"serve-the-quote / prove-don't-guess\" is\n     3\tONE implementation, not three. It performs the two per-atom checks the store's `verify()` does for\n     4\tthe whole log, on a single record:\n     5\t\n     6\t  1. BINDING — the record's content still hashes to its stored `cert_digest` (catches a silent\n     7\t     payload edit).\n     8\t  2. DERIVATION — `entry_hash` is correctly derived from (seq, prev_hash, cert_digest) (catches an\n     9\t     entry-field tamper).\n    10\t\n    11\tCross-record LINKAGE (prev_hash == the predecessor's entry_hash) needs the predecessor and is done\n    12\tby `SpineTailer` as records stream. Reuses `reuse.digest_payload` and the canonical `_entry_hash`\n    13\tfrom `reuse.chain` verbatim — never a re-implementation that could drift from the enforced path.\n    14\t\n    15\tSCOPE (honest): these are UNKEYED sha-256 checks. They catch accidental corruption and a naive\n    16\tstale-field tamper, but they do NOT prove AUTHENTICITY against a writer who can recompute the\n    17\tdigests (a tip tamper or a forward-cascaded fork stays internally consistent). Resistance to that\n    18\trequires the owner-SIGNED head — `SpineTailer.check_anchor` (`checkpoint.classify_head`/`verify_head`),\n    19\twhich is what marks a record `anchored`. Treat a passing `verify_record` as well-formedness, not proof.\"\"\"\n    20\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    21\t\n    22\tfrom ..reuse import digest_payload\n    23\tfrom ..reuse.chain import _entry_hash\n    24\t\n    25\t\n    26\tdef verify_record(record) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n    27\t    \"\"\"(ok, reason) for a single SpineRecord — binding + entry-hash derivation. Fail-closed.\"\"\"\n    28\t    content = {\n    29\t        \"scope\": record.scope, \"kind\": record.kind, \"source\": record.source, \"actor\": record.actor,\n    30\t        \"payload\": record.payload, \"parent_id\": record.parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": record.supersedes_id,\n    31\t    }\n    32\t    if digest_payload(content) != record.cert_digest:\n    33\t        return False, f\"binding break at seq {record.seq}: payload does not match cert_digest (record tampered)\"\n    34\t    if _entry_hash(record.seq, record.prev_hash, record.cert_digest) != record.entry_hash:\n    35\t        return False, f\"entry_hash mismatch at seq {record.seq}: derivation broken (entry tampered)\"\n    36\t    return True, f\"seq {record.seq} binds and derives cleanly\"\n===== sigil/spine/tail.py =====\n     1\t\"\"\"SpineTailer (Phase 7, P0.2) — a live tail over the append-only, poll-only spine with an HONEST,\n     2\ttwo-layer integrity model (red-pen-hardened: unkeyed hashes alone cannot resist a writer who can\n     3\trecompute them):\n     4\t\n     5\t  • `integrity_ok` (CHEAP, per-poll, unkeyed) — per-record binding+derivation (`verify_record`) plus\n     6\t    cross-record LINKAGE (this record's `prev_hash` == the last emitted `entry_hash`). This catches\n     7\t    ACCIDENTAL corruption, a naive stale-field tamper, a deletion/reorder/gap. It does NOT resist a\n     8\t    file-writer who recomputes cert_digest+entry_hash (a tip tamper or a forward-cascaded fork stays\n     9\t    internally consistent) — so it is necessary but not sufficient, and is never presented as proof\n    10\t    of authenticity on its own.\n    11\t\n    12\t  • `anchored` (KEYED, via `check_anchor`) — the owner-SIGNED head (`checkpoint.classify_head` /\n    13\t    `verify_head`, Ed25519 1-of-1 trust root, monotonic `last_seq`) notarizes the prefix\n    14\t    [0 .. signed_last_seq]. A recompute-fork or truncation AT OR BELOW the signed head is\n    15\t    unforgeable without the owner key and is caught here; a monotonic high-water catches a rollback\n    16\t    of even the un-notarized tail. Records with seq > signed_last_seq are the FRESH, not-yet-keyed\n    17\t    tail — emitted `anchored=False` (well-formed but not tamper-proof), keyed at the next `sigil sign`.\n    18\t\n    19\tA consumer (UI/mobile) shows `integrity_ok=False` as \"integrity broken\", and treats only\n    20\t`anchored=True` records as owner-notarized truth; the un-notarized tail is labelled as such, never\n    21\tdressed up as proven. One primitive, two consumers — the UI SSE feed and the mobile push notifier —\n    22\tboth drive `poll()` on a tick and fan events out via `Broadcaster`.\"\"\"\n    23\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    24\t\n    25\tfrom collections import deque\n    26\tfrom typing import Optional\n    27\t\n    28\tfrom ..config import HEAD_PATH\n    29\tfrom ..reuse import SignedChainHead\n    30\tfrom ..reuse.chain import _GENESIS_PREV\n    31\tfrom .checkpoint import classify_head, trust_root\n    32\tfrom .store import SpineStore\n    33\tfrom .verify import verify_record\n    34\t\n    35\t\n    36\tdef _shape(record, *, integrity_ok: bool, integrity_reason: str, anchored: bool) -> dict:\n    37\t    \"\"\"The cited atom shape emitted to consumers. `integrity_ok` = unkeyed well-formedness;\n    38\t    `anchored` = covered by the owner-signed head (keyed). `text` is best-effort, never fabricated.\"\"\"\n    39\t    return {\n    40\t        \"seq\": record.seq, \"kind\": record.kind, \"source\": record.source, \"actor\": record.actor,\n    41\t        \"ts\": record.ts, \"entry_hash\": record.entry_hash, \"text\": record.text(),\n    42\t        \"integrity_ok\": integrity_ok, \"integrity_reason\": integrity_reason, \"anchored\": anchored,\n    43\t    }\n    44\t\n    45\t\n    46\tclass SpineTailer:\n    47\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, since_seq: int = -1,\n    48\t                 signed_head: Optional[SignedChainHead] = None, tr=None):\n    49\t        \"\"\"Emit records with seq > `since_seq`. `signed_head`/`tr` may be injected (tests); otherwise\n    50\t        the owner-signed head is loaded from `HEAD_PATH` + the persisted trust root.\"\"\"\n    51\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n    52\t        self.cursor = since_seq\n    53\t        if since_seq < 0:\n    54\t            self._last_hash = _GENESIS_PREV\n    55\t        else:\n    56\t            anchor = self.store.get(since_seq)\n    57\t            self._last_hash = anchor.entry_hash if anchor else _GENESIS_PREV\n    58\t        self._injected_head = signed_head\n    59\t        self._injected_tr = tr\n    60\t        self._high_water = -1                           # monotonic anti-rollback water mark\n    61\t        self._signed_last_seq = -1\n    62\t        self.check_anchor()                             # establish the initial keyed anchor (reads disk)\n    63\t\n    64\t    def poll(self) -> list[dict]:\n    65\t        \"\"\"Newly-appended records (seq > cursor), each with the cheap `integrity_ok` verdict and the\n    66\t        `anchored` (keyed) flag from the last `check_anchor`. On an integrity failure the event is\n    67\t        emitted flagged (not dropped); the cursor still advances so the feed never re-emits or stalls.\"\"\"\n    68\t        out: list[dict] = []\n    69\t        for r in self.store.iter_records(since_seq=self.cursor):\n    70\t            atom_ok, reason = verify_record(r)\n    71\t            if r.prev_hash != self._last_hash:\n    72\t                ok = False\n    73\t                reason = f\"linkage break at seq {r.seq}: prev_hash != last emitted entry_hash (rewind/fork/gap)\"\n    74\t            else:\n    75\t                ok = atom_ok\n    76\t            out.append(_shape(r, integrity_ok=ok, integrity_reason=reason,\n    77\t                              anchored=(r.seq <= self._signed_last_seq)))\n    78\t            self.cursor = r.seq\n    79\t            self._last_hash = r.entry_hash\n    80\t        return out\n    81\t\n    82\t    def check_anchor(self) -> dict:\n    83\t        \"\"\"The KEYED verdict. Verify the owner-signed head over the current chain (unforgeable without\n    84\t        the owner key): a recompute-fork or truncation at/below the signed head → `anchor_ok=False`;\n    85\t        a monotonic high-water rollback of even the un-notarized tail → `rollback` set. Updates\n    86\t        `signed_last_seq` so `poll()` can flag records beyond it as the un-notarized tail.\"\"\"\n    87\t        entries = self.store.entries()                  # FRESH read from disk (not the cached head)\n    88\t        head_seq = entries[-1].seq if entries else -1\n    89\t        rollback = None\n    90\t        if head_seq < self._high_water:\n    91\t            rollback = f\"ROLLBACK: on-disk head seq {head_seq} < monotonic high-water {self._high_water}\"\n    92\t        else:\n    93\t            self._high_water = head_seq\n    94\t        head, tr = self._resolve_head()\n    95\t        if head is None:\n    96\t            self._signed_last_seq = -1\n    97\t            return {\"anchor_ok\": False, \"signed_last_seq\": -1, \"rollback\": rollback,\n    98\t                    \"reason\": \"no signed checkpoint — the live tail is well-formed but UN-NOTARIZED \"\n    99\t                              \"(run `sigil sign` to anchor)\"}\n   100\t        try:\n   101\t            ok, reason = classify_head(head, entries, tr)\n   102\t        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — a malformed head must FAIL closed, never crash the feed\n   103\t            self._signed_last_seq = -1\n   104\t            return {\"anchor_ok\": False, \"signed_last_seq\": -1, \"rollback\": rollback,\n   105\t                    \"reason\": f\"anchor unverifiable ({e})\"}\n   106\t        self._signed_last_seq = head.last_seq if ok else -1\n   107\t        return {\"anchor_ok\": ok and rollback is None, \"signed_last_seq\": self._signed_last_seq,\n   108\t                \"rollback\": rollback, \"reason\": reason}\n   109\t\n   110\t    def _resolve_head(self):\n   111\t        if self._injected_head is not None:\n   112\t            return self._injected_head, self._injected_tr\n   113\t        try:\n   114\t            if not HEAD_PATH.exists():\n   115\t                return None, None\n   116\t            head = SignedChainHead.model_validate_json(HEAD_PATH.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n   117\t            return head, trust_root()\n   118\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — no/broken head → unkeyed live tail (honest, fail-closed)\n   119\t            return None, None\n   120\t\n   121\t\n   122\tclass Broadcaster:\n   123\t    \"\"\"Fan-out of tail events to N subscribers with bounded per-subscriber queues. On overflow the\n   124\t    oldest events are dropped and the subscriber is marked `lagged` so it resyncs from the cursor\n   125\t    (never a fabricated 'you saw everything').\"\"\"\n   126\t    def __init__(self, maxlen: int = 512):\n   127\t        self.maxlen = maxlen\n   128\t        self._subs: dict[int, deque] = {}\n   129\t        self._lagged: dict[int, bool] = {}\n   130\t        self._next_id = 0\n   131\t\n   132\t    def subscribe(self) -> int:\n   133\t        sid = self._next_id\n   134\t        self._next_id += 1\n   135\t        self._subs[sid] = deque(maxlen=self.maxlen)\n   136\t        self._lagged[sid] = False\n   137\t        return sid\n   138\t\n   139\t    def unsubscribe(self, sid: int) -> None:\n   140\t        self._subs.pop(sid, None)\n   141\t        self._lagged.pop(sid, None)\n   142\t\n   143\t    def publish(self, events: list[dict]) -> None:\n   144\t        for sid, q in self._subs.items():\n   145\t            for ev in events:\n   146\t                if len(q) == self.maxlen:        # would drop the oldest → the subscriber lagged\n   147\t                    self._lagged[sid] = True\n   148\t                q.append(ev)\n   149\t\n   150\t    def drain(self, sid: int) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:\n   151\t        \"\"\"Return (events, lagged) and clear both. `lagged=True` tells the consumer to resync.\"\"\"\n   152\t        q = self._subs.get(sid)\n   153\t        if q is None:\n   154\t            return [], False\n   155\t        events = list(q)\n   156\t        q.clear()\n   157\t        lagged = self._lagged.get(sid, False)\n   158\t        self._lagged[sid] = False\n   159\t        return events, lagged\n===== sigil/agents/kernel_classify.py =====\n     1\t\"\"\"KernelClassifier (Phase 7, P0.1) — the Python↔Rust WARDEN bridge. The authoritative danger\n     2\tclassifier is Rust `kernel/src/tiers.rs::classify` (token-based, danger-first, fail-closed to A3),\n     3\tcomposed with the raise-only registry pins in `Warden::decide`.
